chunks: The most rightful of people to step forward in congregational prayer is the best reciter of the Quran among them. If they are equal in recitation, then the one senior-most in hijra. If they are equal in hijra, then the oldest of them. If they are equal in age, then the most comely in face.

The owner of the mosque has the most right to his mosque. And whoever leads a group in prayer while among them is one more learned than him, their affair does not cease to decline until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.أقرأ: Best in Quran recitation — the primary qualification for leading prayer
key_terms.سفال: Decline, abasement — the consequence of appointing a less qualified imam
key_terms.هجرة: Hijra — migration for the sake of faith, a measure of religious dedication

ai.seo_question: Who has the most right to lead congregational prayer in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling on who has the right to lead congregational prayer (salat al-jama'a), presenting a clear priority hierarchy: Quran recitation ability, seniority in hijra (migration for the faith), age, and then physical appearance. This reflects early Islamic communal values where knowledge of Quran was considered the highest qualification for religious leadership. The final warning — that a community's affairs will decline if they appoint an imam less learned than others — serves as a deterrent against improper appointment and emphasizes the importance of scholarly qualification in religious leadership.
